result.summary: Pausanias describes the sanctuary of the Great Goddesses at Megalopolis, with its statues, tables, temples and rules of entry. He then notes a gymnasium, two hills with ruined temples behind the portico of Philip, and the spring Bathyllus.

scenes.title: Sanctuary of the Great Goddesses
scenes.summary: Pausanias lists the statues, reliefs and temples in the precinct, including those of Demeter, Proserpine, Friendly Zeus and Aphrodite, and notes who may enter.

scenes.title: Gymnasium, hills and spring
scenes.summary: Pausanias mentions the gymnasium, the two hills with ruined temples of Athene and Hera, and the spring Bathyllus feeding the Helisson.

notable_quotes.reason: Pausanias gives his opinion that most inventions come from Aphrodite.

analysis.text: The passage shows Pausanias' interest in local cult, statues and the identity of the gods worshipped by Arcadians.
The Great Goddesses' rites at Megalopolis imitated the Eleusinian Mysteries, showing how mystery cults spread in Greece.

fun_facts.text: Pausanias says the sculptor Damophon made several statues here; he was from Messene.

language_notes.text: Refers to Pausanias' earlier account of Messenia (Book 4), where he discussed the cult and mysteries of the Great Goddesses.
A cubit is roughly the length of a forearm, about 18 inches (0.45 m), so this Hercules is a small figure.
The Idæan Dactyli were legendary Cretan beings, 'Fingers' of Mount Ida, associated with metalworking and the infant Zeus. Onomacritus was an early compiler of oracles and verse.
Buskins are high laced boots; a thyrsus is a staff topped with a pine cone, carried by Dionysus and his followers.
'Square figures' are herms: four-sided pillars, usually topped with a head, rather than fully carved statues.
Fillets are ribbons or woollen bands tied round statues and altars as offerings.
'Full-grown' translates Hera's cult title Teleia, meaning 'perfect' or 'complete', often linked to her role as wife.

context_notes.text: Damophon of Messene was a celebrated sculptor of the second century BC who made many cult statues in the Peloponnese.
Polycletus of Argos was a famous fifth-century BC sculptor, best known for his bronze athletes.
The Eleusinian Mysteries were Athens' secret rites of Demeter and Proserpine (Persephone), promising a happier afterlife to initiates.
Megalopolis was founded in the 370s BC as the Arcadian capital; the Helisson was the river running through it.

literary_notes.text: Water trickling from the nymphs' jars gives a vivid, almost moving picture of the carved table.
Pausanias notes the eagle as the single discordant detail with dry restraint, showing his critical eye as an antiquarian.
Pausanias' personal 'in my opinion' shows his habit of rationalizing cult titles, here praising Aphrodite's role in human invention.
